newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes weak on short-cover dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes weak on short-cover dlr demand.

text.p: Mexico's peso closed weak on Tuesday after some players speculated against others who needed to cover shorts in dollars, traders said.

"It was a very speculative session, such as we haven't seen in a while. Some foreign dealers used the Indian Congress as a pretext to put pressure on the peso and withhold dollars from local dealers who needed to cover shorts," said Pablo Perrusquia, a trader at the Inverlat brokerage.

The National Indian Congress was due to begin Tuesday afternoon in Mexico City, and caused some controversy when rebel leaders from the state of Chiapas expressed their intention to attend against government wishes.

The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 1.9 and 2.1 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.5450/7.5480 and 7.5420/7.5460 per dollar. The same-day peso earlier closed 1.2 centavos weaker at 7.5280/7.5380.
"Also, as often happens on a Tuesday, there were some who sold dollars to take part in the primary Cetes auction," Perrusquia.
A Reuters survey of ten money market traders showed they expected the bellwether 28-day Cetes to fall by an average of 22 basis points to 22.84 percent.
"Even though (the Cetes) rates should fall a bit, they won't weaken the peso. Some of us feel interest rates won't really bottom out until next week," said a trader.
"As trading has been very thin and between few dealers, we cannot measure the full impact, but we do expect the rest of the week to be calm," he added.
